title: Bubble and Squeak
subtitle: Fried potato and cabbage cakes from leftover vegetables
excerpt: Leftover mashed potato and cooked cabbage or sprouts shaped into cakes and fried in a hot pan until crisp on both sides. The traditional British way to use Christmas or Sunday-dinner leftovers.
sourceNotes: Eliza Acton, Modern Cookery for Private Families (1845), Project Gutenberg. Bubble and squeak entries: boiled beef fried with cabbage in the original eighteenth-century version; the modern potato-and-cabbage version became standard in the nineteenth century as potatoes became the dominant leftover. Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), Project Gutenberg #10136.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The uncooked cakes can be shaped and refrigerated for up to 8 hours before frying.

glossaryTerms.definition: Named for the sounds the dish makes as it fries. The bubbling comes from the moisture in the potato and the squeaking from the cabbage contracting in the hot fat.

content.text: turns leftover mashed potato and cooked cabbage or Brussels sprouts into crisp potato cakes. The name comes from the sounds it makes in the pan. The key is a hot pan and enough fat to get a proper crust: pale, steamed cakes are the failure mode. These are best eaten straight from the pan while the crust is still firm.

The mixture needs to be stiff enough to hold a shape when pressed into a cake. If the mash is very soft or the cabbage very wet, it will fall apart in the pan. Squeeze any excess moisture from the cabbage before adding it.

items.prepNote: cooked and cooled, or cooked Brussels sprouts, roughly chopped

content.text: If using onion, fry it gently in a little butter for 5 minutes until soft, then cool. Squeeze any excess water from the cooked cabbage or sprouts.

Mix the {{potato}} of cold mashed potato with the {{cabbage-savoy}} of chopped cooked cabbage (and the onion if using) in a large bowl. Season well with salt and pepper. The mixture should hold together when pressed.
Divide into 8 equal portions. Shape each into a flat cake about 1.5 cm thick.

Heat the butter and oil together in a frying pan over medium-high heat until the butter foams. Add the cakes in a single layer. Do not move them for 4 to 5 minutes: you need a crust to form before you try to flip them.
Flip carefully with a spatula and cook on the other side for another 4 to 5 minutes until golden. Serve at once.

rows.cause: Too much moisture in the cabbage, or mash too soft
rows.fix: Squeeze the cabbage dry in a clean cloth before mixing. Chill the shaped cakes for 30 minutes before frying, which helps them firm up.

rows.cause: Attempting to flip before a crust has formed
rows.fix: Leave the cakes undisturbed for the full 4 to 5 minutes. They will release naturally once the crust has set. If they still resist, give them another minute.

content.text: Bubble and squeak has been made in British kitchens for at least two hundred years, originally as a way to use the boiled beef and vegetables left from the main meal. The beef dropped out in the nineteenth century and the potato-and-cabbage version took over. It is now most strongly associated with the day after Christmas or a Sunday roast, when there are always leftover mashed potatoes and braised greens that need using.
